newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Slightly weaker in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Slightly weaker in slow trade.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market moved slightly down again on Thursday and traders noted decreasing buying interest from a local trading company.
The 180-cst grade for early August lifting was traded at $95.50 per tonne, compared with $96 on Wednesday.
Interest in the 380-cst grade, which was traded at $94 per tonne on Wednesday, was thin and no deals were heard done.
Traders differed in views, with some saying supplies were ample to depress prices while others seeing limited room for further falls.
"The Singapore market should not be too bad because other (fuel oil) markets are pretty firm," said one trader.
Singapore's weekly residues stocks fell by 596,000 barrels to 11.934 million in the week ending July 16, further reinforcing some belief that further falls would be limited.
On demand side, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Thursday it has issued a tender to buy 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil for September delivery.
The tender, which sought a 38,000-tonne low-pour cargo for September 1-15 and a high-pour cargo for September 11-30, closes on July 22 and is valid for two days.
Late on Thursday, the SIMEX fuel oil futures August contract was traded $1 down to $98.00.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
